The PKGBUILD is a standard Arch Linux package recipe for a prebuilt AppImage of the wifi-heatmapper application. It fetches the AppImage from the project's official GitHub release page (https://github.com/hnykda/wifi-heatmapper), which is consistent with the stated upstream source. The SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for the v0.6.0 release, ensuring integrity.

The build process does not compile any code. Instead, it installs the AppImage to `/opt`, creates a symlink in `/usr/bin`, and extracts desktop and icon assets from the AppImage using the `--appimage-extract` feature. This is a common and safe practice for AppImage packaging in AUR. The extracted files (desktop entry and icons) are installed to their standard system locations, and a minor sed edit adjusts the `StartupWMClass` to ensure proper window matching under GTK/Wayland — all of which are benign and user-friendly packaging steps.

There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network access, or execution of downloaded scripts. All operations are transparent, confined to the package build environment, and aligned with standard AUR packaging practices for binary wrappers. The use of `!strip` is appropriate for a binary-only package. No malicious behavior or supply-chain risks are evident.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO is pure package metadata — it contains no executable code, no install scripts, and no post-install hooks. The single source is the project's own GitHub release AppImage (WiFi.Heatmapper_0.6.0_amd64.AppImage), downloaded over HTTPS from the package's declared upstream repository, and pinned with a concrete SHA-256 checksum (e43c5311baa827daa09af323bbce1f22fecbdbfa05ff39b8e3cc935c2561fbd5) so the fetched binary is verified at build time.

The dependencies are consistent with the application's stated purpose of measuring Wi-Fi signal strength and drawing heat maps: networkmanager and iw are needed to query Wi-Fi/network state, webkit2gtk-4.1 provides the GUI toolkit, and fuse2 mounts the AppImage. The optdepends on iperf3 matches the documented throughput-measurement feature. As with any prebuilt (-bin) package, the binary itself cannot be source-audited from this metadata alone, but the pinned checksum and official upstream source are standard AUR practice. Nothing here attempts to exfiltrate data, download code from unexpected hosts, or modify the system outside normal packaging.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
